ask: a successful ask returns the typed answers, model, usage, and duration
a typed failure comes back as data, with pi-typesafe's own code and message
an unknown failure is replaced by a fixed message so nothing from the transport escapes
the ask deadline and the caller's signal both cancel the request
auth: no key at all is an error the consumer cannot mistake for a working setup
another backend reports its own key and never the TypeSafe login hint
an environment key is usable but unverified until something proves it
a rejected key degrades loudly and a later success clears it
a non-authentication failure degrades the signal without pretending the key is gone
a stored key readable by other users is reported as unusable, never as enabled
a corrupt auth record is ignored and clearing forgets both facts
backends: a commandcode request goes to the Command Code path with its own key and model
a per-request model on commandcode is sent unchanged
a caller-supplied endpoint sends to its own path with its own key and unmapped model
an endpoint without a path uses the SDK's own /v1/systemone
an endpoint may use a loopback http: host
an endpoint label must be a nonempty string of at most 60 characters
an endpoint host must be an absolute https: URL with no user info, path, query, or fragment
an endpoint path must be a string that starts with "/"
an endpoint modelsPath must be a string that starts with "/"
an endpoint modelsField must be a nonempty string
an endpoint modelsIdField must be a nonempty string
an endpoint modelsVerifyKey must be a boolean
an endpoint keyEnv must name an environment variable
an endpoint keyEnv must not be TYPESAFE_API_KEY
an endpoint defaultModel must be a nonempty string of at most 100 characters
an endpoint with no defaultModel needs model on createTypeSafe
backend must be a registry name or a backend object
authState refuses an invalid backend instead of reporting a status
an endpoint never reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY or the login store
commandcode with no COMMANDCODE_API_KEY is missing and unusable
a request to an endpoint carries its own key, never the TypeSafe key
a public model list on commandcode leaves the auth state unverified
a model list on an endpoint without modelsVerifyKey leaves the auth state unverified
an endpoint with modelsVerifyKey true records verification
a successful evaluate records verification even after a public model list
a malformed reply on commandcode is a response error
a malformed reply on an endpoint is a response error
401 advice names each backend's own key variable
resolveBackend resolves registry names to the registry entries
backendHost reports the destination host
batch: fan-out bounds concurrency, preserves order, and never throws
fan-out stops launching after a stop rule and marks the rest skipped
fan-out stops launching once the caller's signal aborts
the splitter is pure: a request that already fits is one chunk, unchanged
an invalid request is one settled failure, not a thrown error
more questions than one request may carry are split in order
evaluateAll spends one request per chunk and merges answers, usage, and model
evaluateMany reports per-request failures and stops submitting after a budget error
a daily cap stops the batch with the cap named
calibrate: AUC is the rank-based probability that a positive outranks a negative
a threshold row counts every case once
the default threshold grid is every distinct score, ascending
a recommendation honours the floors, and the report names what it misses and flags
with no floors, the recommendation is the best F1 among the rows
replay scores labelled cases with bounded concurrency and keeps per-case order
a budget failure stops the replay and leaves the rest unsubmitted
replay reports scorer failures with the caller's own message
client: official SDK helpers, typed answers, metadata, and one batched network call
structured state, descriptions, and null values are supported
invalid questions are rejected before network submission without echoing state
validation errors name the offending path, never the submitted value
normalization accepts common model near-misses without loosening the schema
non-JSON state, getters, cycles, and excessive nesting are rejected
UTF-8 byte limit applies before submission
request budget is shared across concurrent calls and failures
HTTP errors are classified, never retried, and do not expose response secrets
HTTP advice names the backend's key, covers 402, and quotes a numeric Retry-After
safeError keeps its one-argument form and defaults the key advice
cancellation before submission does not consume an attempt
in-flight cancellation and timeout reach the transport
malformed successful responses fail safely
client ignores SDK endpoint and logging environment overrides
configuration errors are early and usage snapshots are detached
request data is snapshotted before asynchronous work
evaluate admits the same near-miss aliases as the agent tool
unknown backend throws configuration error
known backend is called at its full request URL
listModels asks each backend for its own model list
a model list without the backend's declared field keeps the SDK's own shape error
the model list is renamed only for the backend that declares another field
a public model list leaves the auth state unverified
the model in the request body is the backend's own id form
a per-request model gets the same mapping as the client default
a TypeSafe key is never sent to another backend
key resolution picks the right env var per backend
credentials: credentials live under Pi's agent directory
store, read, and clear with owner-only permissions
environment variable takes precedence over the stored key
implausible keys are rejected without saving
group- or world-readable credential files are refused
corrupt or unexpected files are treated as no key
createTypeSafe uses the stored key and listModels verifies it without spending the request budget
invalid keys fail verification with a safe message
keySituation is total and names every kind
keySituation for another backend reads only that backend's variable, never the TypeSafe store
extension: Pi loads a tool, a slash command, and a result renderer without network calls
setup and status never display the API key
status names the model the configured backend actually sends
login refuses to shadow an environment key
declining consent keeps the tool disabled
explicit consent enables the real registered tool and returns structured results
disable stops future calls without resetting usage
invalid playground JSON and cancellation do not submit data
playground validates questions before requesting consent
test command requires confirmation and does not enable agent calls
login verifies, stores with owner-only permissions, and never echoes the key
new sessions reset opt-in; headless opt-in is explicit
an enabled session with no key announces that judgments are skipped
a rejected key is called out once per session and shows up in status
the registered tool admits the same near-miss aliases as the library
key-prompt: typed key is masked on screen and returned on Enter
falls back to Pi's plain input when custom UI is unavailable
login: loginWithPrompt cancels cleanly, rejects bad keys, and stores a verified key with owner-only permissions
loginWithPrompt refuses when the environment key would shadow the store, or without a UI
ensureApiKey reports an existing key without prompting, otherwise logs in
ensureApiKey for another backend uses its environment variable and never opens the TypeSafe login
schema: admission accepts the near-miss aliases the agent tool has always accepted
admission enforces the byte budget on the serialized request
the default byte budget is 64 KiB
every field the agent authors carries a description, so a bare union is not its only guidance
usage: a ledger counts requests, tokens, and failures, and prices input tokens only
totals survive a new ledger instance, so a restart does not reset the day
the day rolls over on the local date and old days are kept
each cap stops the next request and names itself
caps come from the environment without ever raising the explicit cap
a corrupt, unreadable, or foreign ledger never blocks a request
the default usage path sits with the key store
